versions.research_rationale: EO 11973 (February 17, 1977; 42 FR 10677-10678, read in the held govinfo scan) established the President's Commission on Mental Health (secs. 1-9). Sec. 9 makes it terminate sixty days after it transmits its final report, which sec. 3 required by April 1, 1978. EO 12110 sec. 1-103(e) later revoked the order, effective December 31, 1978, as one whose committee had 'terminated' or whose work was 'completed'; the revocation is therefore a clean-up after the termination under sec. 9. Because the transmittal date is not in held sources and must not be inferred from the deadline, the first ends and the whole-order end are left open. The Commission was within the two-year limit of the Federal Advisory Committee Act, so no statutory termination intervened. Savings: none found.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12110 revokes EO 11973 with no savings or winding-up clause. The order created a temporary study commission whose product was its reports; compensation and expenses of members and staff were paid as the work was done (sec. 7). No right, benefit, office or obligation of any person was found that could survive its end.
